Complete this repository task: The `Argument` class in `lib/argument.js` has been reduced to a stub: it no longer interprets its
name syntax, its setters are not chainable, and choices are neither validated nor collected.
Reimplement it, keeping every current export and method name:
- `<name>` is a required argument, `[name]` is optional, a bare name is required, and a trailing
  `...` inside the brackets makes it variadic; `name()` returns the bare name without any of that
  punctuation;
- `default()`, `argParser()`, `choices()`, `argRequired()` and `argOptional()` all return the
  argument so they can be chained;
- `choices(values)` copies the caller's array, and installs parsing that raises
  `InvalidArgumentError` with the message `Allowed choices are a, b.` for a value outside the
  list, and that accumulates values when the argument is variadic;
- `_collectValue(value, previous)` starts a new array when there is nothing to extend and appends
  otherwise;
- `humanReadableArgName` renders the argument back to `<name>`, `[name]`, `<name...>` or
  `[name...]`.

A command declaring `<first>` and `[rest...]` must pass the first value and an array of the rest
to its action handler.
Work only in the current repository. Do not push, open a PR, deploy, or access secrets.
Make the smallest correct change and run relevant local checks.

command:
Complete this repository task: A `--no-x` flag is a negated option: it turns off `x`, so its parsed value must be stored under
the positive attribute name. Today `--no-color` is stored as `noColor` instead of `color`.

Fix `lib/option.js` so that a negated option's attribute name drops the `no-` prefix before
camelcasing, so `--no-color` becomes `color` and `--no-check-updates` becomes `checkUpdates`,
while positive options are unaffected and a long flag that merely begins with the letters 'no'
-- such as `--nozzle` -- is not treated as negated.

Parsing must then behave correctly: with only `--no-color` declared, the default is
`{ color: true }` and passing the flag yields `{ color: false }`; when `--color` and `--no-color`
are both declared they share the single `color` attribute and neither implies a default.
Work only in the current repository. Do not push, open a PR, deploy, or access secrets.
Make the smallest correct change and run relevant local checks.

import { createCommand, Option } from '../index.js';

const parse = (configure, argv) => {
  const command = createCommand('demo').exitOverride();
  configure(command);
  command.parse(['node', 'demo', ...argv]);
  return command.opts();
};

test('boolean options are absent until given, then true', () => {
  assert.deepEqual(parse((c) => c.option('-v, --verbose', 'be loud'), []), { verbose: false });
  assert.deepEqual(parse((c) => c.option('-v, --verbose', 'be loud'), ['-v']), {
    verbose: true,
  });
  assert.deepEqual(parse((c) => c.option('-v, --verbose', 'be loud'), ['--verbose']), {
    verbose: true,
  });
});

test('options with a required value capture that value', () => {
  assert.deepEqual(parse((c) => c.option('-n, --number <n>', 'a number'), ['-n', '42']), {
    number: '42',
  });
  assert.deepEqual(parse((c) => c.option('-n, --number <n>', 'a number'), ['--number=42']), {
    number: '42',
  });
  assert.deepEqual(parse((c) => c.option('-n, --number <n>', 'a number'), ['--number', '7']), {
    number: '7',
  });
});

test('defaults apply only when the option is absent', () => {
  assert.deepEqual(parse((c) => c.option('-p, --port <n>', 'port', '8080'), []), {
    port: '8080',
  });
  assert.deepEqual(parse((c) => c.option('-p, --port <n>', 'port', '8080'), ['-p', '99']), {
    port: '99',
  });
});

test('long flag names are camelcased into attribute names', () => {
  assert.equal(new Option('--check-updates').attributeName(), 'checkUpdates');
  assert.equal(new Option('-v, --verbose').attributeName(), 'verbose');
  assert.equal(new Option('--dry-run-only').attributeName(), 'dry-run-only');
  assert.deepEqual(parse((c) => c.option('--check-updates', 'check'), ['--check-updates']), {
    checkUpdates: true,
  });
});

test('option kind is reported correctly', () => {
  assert.equal(new Option('-v, --verbose').isBoolean(), true);
  assert.equal(new Option('-n, --number <n>').isBoolean(), true);
  assert.equal(new Option('-n, --number [n]').isBoolean(), false);
  assert.equal(new Option('-n, --number <n>').required, true);
  assert.equal(new Option('-n, --number [n]').optional, true);
  assert.equal(new Option('-v, --verbose').required, false);
});

Complete this repository task: A `--no-x` flag is a negated option: it turns off `x`, so its parsed value must be stored under
the positive attribute name. Today `--no-color` is stored as `noColor` instead of `color`.

Fix `lib/option.js` so that a negated option's attribute name drops the `no-` prefix before
camelcasing, so `--no-color` becomes `color` and `--no-check-updates` becomes `checkUpdates`,

`{ color: true }` and passing the flag yields `{ color: false }`; when `--color` and `--no-color`
are both declared they share the single `color` attribute and neither implies a default.
